name: Identity Probe
content:
"""
title: Identity Probe
description: Shows which OpenWebUI user reaches this MCP server and what the access rules grant them. Diagnostic only — reads nothing, changes nothing, and never reports a credential.
author: Torsten Feustel
version: 0.0.4
license: MIT
category: System
"""

import hashlib


def _framework():
    """The spawner's identity modules, or None when running anywhere else.

    The same tool JSON can be installed in OpenWebUI itself, where there is no
    framework to ask — so the import has to be allowed to fail.
    """
    try:
        from app import identity, policy
        return identity, policy
    except ImportError:
        return None


def _fingerprint(secret: str) -> str:
    """First twelve hex characters of the secret's SHA-256.

    Two systems have to agree on one string, and neither may show it. A hash
    prefix settles the question without revealing anything: same twelve
    characters means same secret, different means different — and that is the
    single most common reason a forwarded user fails to verify.
    """
    return hashlib.sha256(secret.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]


class Tools:
    def __init__(self):
        pass

    async def whoami(self) -> str:
        """Who am I to this server? Reports the verified OpenWebUI user.

        Use this while setting up per-user identity: it answers whether the
        user token arrived, who it identified, and what this person is allowed
        to reach. Nothing else — it reads no data and changes nothing.

        It never reports a token, a password or any other credential, so its
        output is safe to paste into a chat or a bug report.
        """
        modules = _framework()
        if modules is None:
            return (
                "Nothing to report: this tool only works inside the MCP spawner, "
                "and its identity modules are not importable here."
            )
        identity, policy = modules
        who = identity.get_current_identity()

        if who is None:
            secret = identity.configured_secret()
            trusts_headers = identity.trust_plain_headers()
            lines = ["No identified user reached this tool."]
            if secret:
                lines.append(f"  expected header: {identity.header_name()}")
                lines.append(f"  shared secret:   configured, fingerprint {_fingerprint(secret)}")
            if trusts_headers:
                lines.append(f"  also accepted:   {identity.PLAIN_HEADERS['sub']} (unsigned)")
            if not secret and not trusts_headers:
                lines.append("  this server can identify nobody: no shared secret, "
                             "and plain headers are not trusted")
            lines.append("")
            # The advice differs per mode; a hint about a fingerprint that does
            # not exist sends the reader looking for the wrong thing.
            if secret:
                lines.append(
                    "Check in this order: the User identity setting of this instance "
                    "(off never looks at any header), then the fingerprint above "
                    "against the secret configured in OpenWebUI — the first twelve "
                    "hex characters of its SHA-256 must be identical. After changing "
                    "the secret, restart this instance; a running one keeps the value "
                    "it started with."
                )
            elif trusts_headers:
                lines.append(
                    "Check in this order: the User identity setting of this instance "
                    "(off never looks at any header), then whether OpenWebUI has "
                    "ENABLE_FORWARD_USER_INFO_HEADERS=true, and finally whether "
                    "anything between the two strips unknown headers."
                )
            else:
                lines.append(
                    "Set a shared secret under Settings, or accept the plain user "
                    "headers there, and restart this instance afterwards."
                )
            return "\n".join(lines)

        # Four sources reach this point, not two, and the difference is the
        # whole answer: a signed token was *proved*, everything else was
        # *assigned*. Deciding this on `who.signed` alone labelled an agent
        # token and a machine identity as unsigned OpenWebUI headers — which
        # sends the reader to check ENABLE_FORWARD_USER_INFO_HEADERS for a
        # setup that never involved OpenWebUI at all.
        proof = {
            identity.SOURCE_TOKEN: "signature, issuer and expiry all checked",
            identity.SOURCE_HEADERS:
                "taken from OpenWebUI's plain headers — UNSIGNED, not verified",
            identity.SOURCE_AGENT:
                "a named agent token — assigned, not proven: whoever holds the "
                "token is this agent",
            identity.SOURCE_MACHINE:
                "this instance's configured machine identity — assigned, not "
                "proven: it stands in for every caller without a login",
        }.get(who.source, who.source or "source unknown")
        lines = [f"Identified user ({proof}):"]
        for label, value in (("sub", who.sub), ("email", who.email),
                             ("name", who.name), ("role", who.role)):
            lines.append(f"  {label:<6} {value or '(empty)'}")

        try:
            rules = policy.rules_for(who)
        except Exception as e:
            lines.append("")
            lines.append(f"Access rules unreadable: {e}")
            lines.append("While that lasts, an instance in required mode refuses everyone.")
            return "\n".join(lines)

        lines.append("")
        if rules is None:
            lines.append("No entry in the access rules for this user.")
            lines.append("An instance in required mode refuses them; optional lets them pass.")
            return "\n".join(lines)

        account = str(rules.get("account") or "")
        lines.append(f"Account for this user: {account or '(none configured)'}")
        instances = rules.get("instances")
        if instances in ("*", True):
            lines.append("Allowed: every tool of every instance")
        elif isinstance(instances, dict) and instances:
            lines.append("Allowed:")
            for instance_id, tools in instances.items():
                if tools in ("*", True):
                    lines.append(f"  {instance_id}: every tool")
                elif isinstance(tools, (list, tuple, set)):
                    lines.append(f"  {instance_id}: {', '.join(sorted(str(t) for t in tools))}")
                else:
                    lines.append(f"  {instance_id}: {tools}")
        else:
            lines.append("Allowed: nothing — the entry lists no instances")
        return "\n".join(lines)
